purpose: Create guide modules through an interactive creative-discovery process that understands the requester's intent, reuses what already exists when useful, and preserves room for unexpected relevant directions without forcing a fixed taxonomy.

module_creation_lifecycle.rule: CREATIVE_DISCOVERY is mandatory for a new guide module or a material reinterpretation. It is not a Bordeaux-specific gate and must happen before the system freezes a route, theme, narrative architecture or production plan.
module_creation_lifecycle.fast_path: If the requester has already expressed a sufficiently precise intent and the system can prove that no material ambiguity remains, CREATIVE_DISCOVERY may be brief but cannot be silently replaced by a predefined template.
module_creation_lifecycle.reuse_path: A request may resolve partly or entirely to existing qualified modules, episodes, extras or cross-guide threads when they materially satisfy the intent. Reuse must preserve provenance and must not masquerade as newly researched material.

creation_discovery.goal: Discover what kind of experience should be created before deciding what the guide is about or how it is structured.
requester_can: describe a place, trip, duration, audience, mood, curiosity or constraint in natural language
express an imprecise desire and ask the system to help shape it
accept, ignore, combine or reformulate suggestions
ask to connect the new guide to guides or stories that already exist
creative_director_should: identify what is already established and what remains open
inspect relevant qualified guide material before proposing unnecessary new generation
propose a small number of context-sensitive creative possibilities when they help the requester think
include at least one unexpected but defensible direction when it materially broadens the creative space
explain important consequences such as duration, depth, production complexity or cross-guide continuity
converge only when the requester's intent is sufficiently clear for research and design to proceed
creation_discovery.exit_condition: A concise creative intent exists that captures audience/context, desired experience, meaningful constraints and any desired continuity with existing guides, while explicitly preserving unresolved choices that can safely remain open.

existing_material_resolution.preference: Reuse or connect qualified material when it genuinely serves the discovered intent; create new material when reuse would distort the experience or leave a material gap.
existing_material_resolution.composition: A new module may compose material from several compatible qualified guides or narrative threads when context and provenance remain intelligible.
existing_material_resolution.no_lock_in: Past guides, prior suggestions and previous user choices are context, never a mandatory thematic profile.

must_not: freeze arbitrary thematic axes merely because they are present in a template
invent a user persona to justify decisions
hide whether material is reused or newly generated

runtime_experience.rule: A finished guide may itself offer free-form visitor exploration and contextual suggestions, but this is separate from the mandatory creation-discovery process and must be justified by the product design.
runtime_experience.default: A qualified guide must remain useful without runtime conversational interaction.

navigation_model.step_navigation: Keep per-step external maps deep links when appropriate.
navigation_model.overview_navigation: A visit may expose one overview_maps_url for the full accepted route.

human_gate.required_when: Two or more materially different creative directions remain legitimate after discovery and their consequences cannot be safely treated as reversible implementation choices.
human_gate.shape: Return a small number of concrete, context-specific alternatives or prototypes. Never substitute a permanent catalog of themes for the requester's free-form intent.
not_required_for: reuse of clearly compatible qualified material
